text:
Eve: Heads up — saw memory climb steadily on a long-chat repro (30k+ tokens). Heap snapshot points at KV cache holding more blocks than expected, many with offsets not divisible by page_size. Suspect alignment bug in compaction/append path.

Maya: Ugh. Can you paste the log lines? are these old or new runtimes?

Eve: Running canary build from yesterday (runtime v2.8.1-canary). Logs:
```
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] kv_cache: append block id=0x7f8a size=4096 token_offset=12345 request_id=abcd
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] kv_cache: page_alloc page_idx=47 base_offset=12288 flags=0x1
[2026-03-15T15:12:04Z] kv_cache: compacted segment id=0x7f8a new_offset=12288
[2026-03-15T15:12:04Z] kv_cache: stale block detected id=0x7f8a token_offset=12345 expected_aligned_offset=12288
```
Repro steps attached minimal: long prompt loop with streaming turned on.

Jon: token_offset=12345 not aligned to 4k boundaries — that smells like we used token counts rather than bytes when computing page alignment. Did compaction accidentally mix units?

Maya: We added a change to compute append_offset = base_offset + token_delta last week in the batching heuristics change. It was supposed to be in tokens for KV index on L2, but conversion to bytes might have been skipped during eviction. PR reference: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3421

dmitri: I just ran the repro and saw cross-request contamination — blocks from previous requests being reused in later requests when a slot is recycled quickly. There are logs with request_id reused: older request id still present in block metadata after eviction.

Eve: Yeah, I see two problems: 1) alignment desync (offsets not rounded to page boundary) and 2) stale request_id not cleared on free -> leads to cross-request leakage during quick slot reuse. Might be the same code path: free() doesn't zero metadata if block is marked tombstone, but fast-path reuse skips zeroing.

Maya: Can we get a small repro script that fails in CI? If we can reproduce deterministically, we should add a unit test for compaction + fast reuse.

Eve: I created a repro harness: loop that allocates, writes random KV frames, and forces eviction via small pool. Repro logs and a short flamegraph from perf attached to the thread:
- wasted CPU around kv::compact_and_merge
- weird branch in append_hot_path where token_delta computation jumps cases

priya: I poked at the code. Suspect spot: kv_store::append_block() uses two code paths depending on "fast_path" flag. The fast path skips calling zero_metadata() for perf. That was an optimization but I think it didn't handle the case where the compacted offset is smaller than prior token_offset due to rounding.

Jon: For immediate mitigation, we can add an assertion in debug builds that token_offset % page_size == 0 after compaction and before reuse. Also ensure free() always clears request_id in non-prod builds.

dmitri: Agreed. I'll open a hotfix PR to zero request_id and to add the debug assert: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3478 (WIP).

Eve: I tried a quick patch locally: zeroing metadata removes cross-request leaks but memory growth still happens — alignment mismatch remains. I hacked a conversion in append path (tokens->bytes) and the memory growth stopped in my local run. So two commits needed.

Maya: We need to check interactions with KV page compaction heuristics — rounding up vs rounding down. If we round down, we might produce smaller offsets and then compaction will attempt to merge resulting fragments incorrectly. We should standardize to always round down to nearest page boundary on alloc, and always round up when computing required space so we don't overlap. Document the invariants.

priya: Also check eviction tombstones: we have an optimization to leave small "ghost" fragments to avoid churn; maybe those are being misinterpreted as live when offsets shift. Add tagging for ghost vs tombstone in the block header (if not present) or at least ensure ghost blocks are never reused without a full reset.

Jon: For the rollout plan:
- hotfix PR to zero request_id + debug asserts (canary today)
- follow-up PR to fix token->byte conversion and add unit tests for alignment and cross-request reuse (tomorrow)
- perf run to ensure no regression on throughput/latency due to zeroing (range test with 1k simultaneous short requests)

Eve: I'll attach the minimal repro and heap diffs to the PR. Also adding a tiny e2e where we ramp tokens to 50k to catch regressions in CI.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for runtime/canary to test PR 3478 — status: queued.

dmitri: If anyone can review PR 3478 quickly that's great — it's small. After that, we'll push canary to a handful of internal environments and monitor memory for long-context traces.

Maya: Thanks all. Let's keep this thread for updates. If we don't see the leak after the fixes, we should still add a periodic KV integrity check job that validates offsets and request_id clearing across the pool.

Eve: Filing an internal follow-up ticket to add the integrity check and docs describing alignment invariant: AR-9876.

priya: I'll start writing unit tests around append_block/compact_and_merge. Ping me for test harness bits.

Jon: Great — assign owners and we'll close after canary passes. :thumbsup:
